chunks: Allah, the Exalted, said: “And give its due on the day of its harvest.”

This means that you take in your hand one bundle after another and give it to the needy person, then another needy person, until you finish from it. At the time of date-cutting, a handful after a handful until you finish from it; and from the gathering, a handful after a handful until you finish from it. And something is left for the guard who is in the orchard as a known wage, and from the palm tree there is left ma‘āfārah and Umm Ja‘rūr, and there is left for the guard one cluster, two clusters, and three for his guarding it.
As for His, the Exalted, saying: “And do not be wasteful; indeed, He does not love the wasteful.”
Then wastefulness is that you give away everything with both your hands.

key_terms.الصِّرَامِ: the time of cutting or harvesting dates
key_terms.الضِّغْثَ: a bundle or handful of gathered stalks
key_terms.الْإِسْرَافُ: wastefulness, here meaning giving away all of it at once
key_terms.الْجِذَاذِ: the cutting and gathering of harvested produce, especially dates
key_terms.الْحَارِسِ: the guard over the orchard or harvest who is given a known wage
key_terms.الْمِسْكِينَ: the needy person who receives from the produce
key_terms.حَصَادِهِ: its harvest time, when the due is to be given
key_terms.حَقَّهُ: the due right owed from the produce at harvest

ai.seo_question: What does “And give its due on the day of its harvest” mean in practice?
ai.summary: This passage explains the meaning of giving the crop’s due at harvest by distributing portions gradually to the needy from the produce as it is collected. It also clarifies that one should leave a known share for the guard, while avoiding excess by not giving away everything at once.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Allah (swt), the Almighty, says: "And give its due on the day of its harvest" (Surah Al-An’am 6:141).

This means that you take handful after handful and give it to the needy, then to another needy person, until you are done. At the time of reaping, you give a handful after another until it is completed. Similarly, from the fruit that is picked, you give handful by handful until finished.
For the guard (over the harvest), you leave a specific wage for their work, and from the palm trees, you leave what is known as ma‘afarah (small dates) and Um J‘arur (inferior dates). Additionally, the guard is allowed to take one, two, or three bunches of dates as compensation for protecting the trees.
As for Allah’s (swt) statement: "But do not be wasteful, for He does not love the wasteful" (Surah Al-An’am 6:141),
wastefulness here refers to giving away all of it with both hands.
